title: Migrate raw dict to dataclass then add validation in Python — 3 turns
description: Raw dict-based code migrated to dataclass, tests kept green, validators added.

files.tests/test_product.py:
import pytest
from product import create_product, get_product_name, get_product_price, update_stock, is_in_stock, format_product


def test_create():
    p = create_product("Widget", 9.99)
    assert get_product_name(p) == "Widget"
    assert get_product_price(p) == 9.99


def test_update_stock():
    p = create_product("Gadget", 4.99, stock=10)
    p = update_stock(p, 5)
    assert p.stock == 15
    p = update_stock(p, -3)
    assert p.stock == 12


def test_is_in_stock():
    p = create_product("Thing", 1.00, stock=0)
    assert not is_in_stock(p)
    p = update_stock(p, 1)
    assert is_in_stock(p)


def test_format():
    p = create_product("Item", 2.50, stock=3)
    assert format_product(p) == "Item: $2.50 (3 in stock)"


def test_validation_negative_price():
    """Should raise ValueError for negative price."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        create_product("Bad", -1.0)


def test_validation_empty_name():
    """Should raise ValueError for empty name."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        create_product("", 9.99)

task_spec.prompt: Migrate `product.py` from raw dicts to a `Product` dataclass. Define `@dataclass class Product` with fields `name: str`, `price: float`, `stock: int = 0`. Update `create_product()` to return a `Product`, and update the other functions to accept `Product` instead of `dict`. The test uses `p.stock` (attribute access), not `p['stock']`. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to confirm tests pass.
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to confirm no regressions. Make sure all attribute accesses work (p.stock, p.name, p.price). Walk me through what changed.

Final pass: add validation in `create_product()` (or in `__post_init__`): raise `ValueError` if name is empty or price is negative. Then run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm everything is green — all 6 tests must pass.
